# The canvas example's five-second block is reported as a wedged update

No contributor labels: the example ships with Engine 14 on Mon 23 Nov, its spec can red an unrelated pull request, and the fix is mine (the example is #21876's).

## Context

Found on 22 Nov in the e2e run of PR #21950 at `28f4c561ca`, job 137262947395, `e2e-engine (1/15)`: `WorkerCanvas.spec.mjs:17` failed on its no-error assertions, because the page console held

```
vdom update wedged: "neo-component-3" has been in-flight for over 5000ms. Its reply was likely lost — the component will not update again, and ancestor updates will yield to it.
```

That diff does not touch the canvas example. Since the example merged at 14:57Z, this is one of 11 finished runs of that shard (counted 15:56Z over every pull request; the two other red ones had passed all 70 tests and hit the step's ceiling).

Live latest-open + closed sweep: checked the latest 20 open plus open and closed searches (`vdom update wedged`, `MainThreadBlocker`, `WorkerCanvas`, `watchdogThreshold`; #18788's and #20747's subjects read) at 2026-11-22T15:57Z; no equivalent and no prior exclusion found. Backlog band: 73 open, red; the leaf that owned the example (#21876) is closed, so this is filed. A2A claims: none on this scope. Memory Core: one query on the symptom, no prior decision. Own open tickets: none on this surface.

## The Problem

`examples/worker/canvas` blocks its window's main thread for five seconds on purpose. The app goes on writing the page clock ten times a second. The write that leaves as the block begins stays in flight until the main thread returns: five seconds, minus the time since the block began, plus the main thread's catch-up. `Neo.manager.VDomUpdate` arms a watchdog of 5,000 ms for every update in flight and logs an error when it fires. So the two five-second spans race, and on a slower machine the watchdog wins.

The update is late, not lost: it settles when the block ends and the clock runs on. But the console says the component "will not update again", on the one example whose claim is that the app keeps running while the page stands. And the spec's assertions that nothing was logged turn the shard red for whoever's pull request ran it.

Design authority: the watchdog's own JSDoc, "Updates settle in milliseconds; the generous default avoids false positives on heavily loaded sessions": a false positive is what it is built to avoid.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/manager/VDomUpdate.mjs`: `watchdogThreshold = 5000` (L127-L133, "Mutable for tests"), read when an update is registered (`#armWatchdog`, L604-L618).
- `examples/worker/canvas/MainContainer.mjs`: `onBlockButtonClick` (L92-L124) knows the block's length before it starts and awaits `Neo.main.addon.MainThreadBlocker.block({duration, windowId})`; `runClock` writes the page clock every 100 ms.
- `test/playwright/e2e/rendering/WorkerCanvas.spec.mjs` asserts an empty console, and the e2e fixture asserts that no worker error reached the page (`fixtures.mjs` L259-L260).

## The Fix

In `onBlockButtonClick`, give the watchdog room for the block the example is about to cause: raise `Neo.manager.VDomUpdate.watchdogThreshold` to at least twice the block's duration before the block, and put it back in `finally`.

The spec gains a test that makes the report certain without the fix: it sets the threshold below the block (4,000 ms) before pressing the button, then asserts that no wedged update is reported and that the threshold is back afterwards.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: With a watchdog threshold of 4,000 ms set before the press, the five-second block reports no wedged update (e2e; red without the fix).
- [ ] AC-2: After the block the threshold is what it was before the press.
- [ ] AC-3: The existing test stays green; the example's page and its copy are unchanged.

## Out of Scope

A public way for an app to tell the engine that its main thread will be away (the example uses the mutable member). The block's length, the page's copy, the catalog record and the cover.

## Avoided Traps

- Shortening the block: the button, the record and the cover say five seconds.
- Pausing the page clock for the block: the app would stop the clock itself, which is the opposite of the proof.
- Listing the error as expected in the spec: a visitor's console would still show it.

## Related
